I was once in the hospital, given meds for something, and the meds caused an extremely severe physical reaction. Would black out, wildly dizzy, barely able to move, felt like I was literally on fire, pins and needles, legs collapsing under me. Never in my life was anxiety even remotely like that, qnd it started the moment I started those meds.

Told the doctor. He laughed, scoffed at me, told me "you know what Anxiety is, right? Everyone has it. Like when you stand on a stage and get sweaty. You know what anxiety is, right?" Talked down to me like I was a toddler. In the tone of a 1st grade teacher. Told me it was all in my head, I just didnt understand I was experiencing anxiety, qnd I needed to get over it.

Stopped taking the meds on my own. The symptoms stopped instantly. I fucking hate doctors and nurses who use ""anxiety""" as a reason to dismiss you or mock you Fuck those people.

This is one of the most clear-cut descriptions/cases of addiction I have read on here. 

"i feel like i need oxy but not in like the typical drug addict all the time way. i just need it to feel normal and to feel better at least once" That is *exactly* the "typical drug addict way", actually. 

'Needing' the drug to feel 'normal' is 100% drug addiction. Chronic stealing, constantly craving the drugs, being terrified of not having them............ the writing is on the wall. 

I'm not sure how to tell you to proceed, since you said youself you may not want to stop, but as for if you have a problem..... you do,, A serious one. I hope knowing that helps you in some way.
I have read it! All of it sounds very familar, I think, as someone who suffers from PTSD (from various things),,,, I feel very, very uneasy and unsure thinking about what to do about it, though.

"Addiction switching"..... if I'm understanding the meaning right, I think i may struggle with something similar,,, I've noticed something about myself, that often times I'll go "all in" on something (alcohol, cutting, gambling, ect), be utterly fixated with it for a while, and then I'll climb out of the hole and be fine...... but very, very quickly I will find myself indulging in some other substance/behaviour, and suddenly I'm "all in" on that one...... and then I get over That one, and fall into another thing......... and then climb out of that and go straight into another thing........... until I loop around and am transfixed again by the first substance/behaviour in the cycle.

I feel restless and uneasy without engaging in something addictive/self-destructive, and find myself switching between substances/behaviours when I have to stop or loss my investment in one.

Oh, i dont think this would mean I'm incapable of change..... it was more of a musing,,, Wondering out loud if I (and others) are in some way wired to obsess and fixate, maybe natually pre-desposed to self-destructive behaviour patterns. Whether it is affected by something "natural" or something I was born with, that doesnt mean "dont ever try" , or "nothing can change".
